subject: Data fencing & keystore escrow: subprocessor notification and operational runbook
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Darren Li <darren.li@acmehealth.com>, legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:50:00 -0800
Subject: Data fencing, escrow triggers, and subproc notification for VPC deployment

Thanks, Jonas — quick summary following our vendor intake call this morning. Acme is moving forward with a private VPC deployment and we need to close three privacy items before procurement: 1) an explicit operational runbook describing how Redwood will notify us before onboarding new subprocessors that will touch tenant metadata or keystore endpoints; 2) the escrow release triggers for customer-managed keys (CMK), including a final list of who can request break-glass access and the audit steps; and 3) a clear data-fencing map (per-region) showing network boundaries and operator access scopes so our security team can sign off.

Can you confirm Redwood's committed notification window for subprocessor changes, and whether you can provide a template attestation we can reuse in our pockets? We also need to understand if any subprocessors will cross-border in the course of HSM rotation or backup exports.

We attached our procurement checklist and a short matrix of required evidence. Happy to jump on a 30m follow-up if that helps.

Attachments: procurement_checklist_acme_1119.pdf (external)

Best,
Elena Morales
Director, InfoSec Procurement
Acme Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data fencing, escrow triggers, and subproc notification for VPC deployment

Elena — thanks for the clear list. High level answers inline: 1) Subprocessor notification: Redwood will provide 30 days' notice for any subprocessor that would have the ability to access tenant-level metadata or keystore endpoints. For emergency/urgent onboarding (rare), we will provide as-early-as-possible notice and a post-hoc attestation. We can provide a reusable attestation template — see attached draft (redline_DPA_acme_v3.pdf).

2) CMK escrow release triggers: Our standard is that escrow release requires a documented request from an authorized customer signatory plus a joint verification call with Redwood ops and the customer's security contact. Break-glass is available for incident response but is guarded by multi-party approval (customer, Redwood security, and our legal team). We propose an escrow release playbook that lists the steps, the logging that will be captured, and a retention schedule for audit evidence. See keystore_escrow_proposal.docx.

3) Data fencing map: will provide a per-region network boundary diagram and an operator access matrix. Short answer: operator access to customer VPC control plane is scoped to ephemeral service accounts that are pinned to a specific Warden pool; no operator has standing host-level access. I will pull the network diagram and the operator demarcation into the Drive folder and share the link.

Proposed next steps:
- I will circulate the redlined DPA and the escrow proposal today.
- Kimberly will review the legal redlines and mark the must-haves vs negotiables.
- Priyom will prepare the subprocessor matrix with geography and function (haas, hsm mgmt, backup storage) and flag any potential cross-border movement.

If that sounds good, can we target Wednesday (24 Nov) for final alignment? I can do 10–11am PT.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline_DPA_acme_v3.pdf; keystore_escrow_proposal.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acmehealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data fencing, escrow triggers, and subproc notification for VPC deployment

Elena/Jonas — attaching a short legal summary and a few targeted redlines. High-level positions:

- Subprocessor notice window: we can commit to 30 days' notice for non-emergency additions. For emergency-only cases (e.g., urgent HSM vendor patching), Redwood will provide immediate notification and a remediation/attestation within 5 business days. This mirrors industry norms but we'll add the attestation template as part of the DPA annex.

- Escrow access: we will not permit escrow release solely on internal Redwood triggers. Escrow release requires (a) customer request from an authorized signer, (b) a joint verification call, and (c) a notarized attestation from Redwood's security lead for the change. For litigation or lawful process, we will require the same customer notice and will log all actions to immutable audit records.

- Data fencing and operator scope: propose adding a short appendix that maps operator roles (network ops, telemetry, keystore ops) to the exact API endpoints they can call, and includes an example Warden pool ID per region. This makes audits easier.

Open questions for Acme: please confirm the internal list of authorized signatories for escrow requests and the required escalation contact. Also confirm whether Acme requires HSM vendor geofencing (we can support onshore-only rotation windows but need to know the acceptable countries).

Attached: redline_summary_kimberly_2323.pdf (legal highlights).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acmehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Darren Li <darren.li@acmehealth.com>, legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data fencing, escrow triggers, and subproc notification for VPC deployment

Thanks, Kimberly/Jonas — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple quick confirmations:

- Acme authorized signatories list attached (separate email) and Darren Li will be primary for escrow requests.
- We require HSM rotations to be onshore-only for the first 12 months; please flag any subprocessor whose operations would cross borders during rotation or backups.
- Wednesday 10:00am PT works. I'll send a calendar invite and include our procurement and cloud architecture leads.

Please bring the attestation template and the operator-role appendix to the call. If Redwood can also surface the subprocessor matrix with a column for "cross-border risk: low/medium/high," that will speed internal approvals.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Elena

Attachments referenced: procurement_checklist_acme_1119.pdf (from initial), authorized_signatories_acme.pdf (external)
